title: The New M6 MacBook Pro Has a Serious Price Problem
gist: Apple's new 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 for 16 GB RAM and 512 GB storage after a $300 price hike earlier in the year, which the reviewer calls poor value. He argues a discounted M6 Mac Mini plus M5 MacBook Air costs the same, and notes Mac Minis are increasingly used as always-on AI agent boxes.

insights.claim: Apple raised prices across all Macs earlier in 2026, with the base 14-inch MacBook Pro hit hardest by a $300 increase, and the M6 version now costs $1,999 for 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Apple is pushing ASPs higher, which may weigh on unit demand for the entry Pro tier.
insights.quote: Apple raised prices across all Macs earlier this year, but the base 14-inch MacBook Pro got hit the hardest, with a $300 bump.

insights.claim: A discounted M6 Mac Mini at $779 plus an M5 MacBook Air about $150 off together cost the same as one M6 MacBook Pro.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Intra-lineup cannibalization: buyers may trade down from the Pro to cheaper Mac combinations.
insights.quote: You could buy both for the same price as one M6 MacBook Pro.

insights.claim: An M5 Pro-chip MacBook Pro for only $200 more offers better performance in an identical chassis, undercutting the base M6 model's value.
